title: Google pauses Gemini image generator after historically inaccurate diverse depictions
description: In February 2024, Google's Gemini AI image-generation feature was found to produce historically and factually inaccurate images — including racially diverse depictions of 1943 German Wehrmacht soldiers and the US Founding Fathers — after users circulated examples publicly. Google attributed the errors to diversity tuning applied without regard for context, combined with an overly cautious prompt-filtering system. Google publicly apologised, calling the results 'embarrassing and wrong,' and paused Gemini's ability to generate images of people while it worked on a fix.

history.note: Initial Phase 2A seed content, part of the Foundational Twenty. The episode unfolded over roughly three days (viral reports ~Feb 20-21, formal apology Feb 23); occurred_date is an approximate midpoint.

root_cause: Fairness/diversity tuning for the image generator was applied indiscriminately, inserting demographic diversity into prompts where historical accuracy required specific, non-diverse depictions, compounded by an overly cautious safety layer that misclassified benign historical prompts as sensitive — and the combination was not caught by pre-release content-safety review across a broad enough range of prompts.

citations.title: Gemini image generation got it wrong. We'll do better.

relationships.reason: A requirement to understand and test the specific context a generative feature will be used in, before broad release, addresses exactly this failure.
This is a prominent example of the reputational risk a generative content feature can create without adequate pre-release review.
